title: Do the two halves behind a dotted line always match?
description: A blue paper triangle and four joined puzzle pieces each have a dotted line down the middle. Folding along each line shows which pair of halves cover each other exactly, and Keeko doubts that any dotted line down the middle gives mirror halves.
teaching_notes: One idea: two halves are mirror halves only when one covers the other exactly after the fold. Watch for students who trust a dotted line, or how equal the sides look, instead of folding.

source: A blue triangle has a dotted line down its middle. If you fold the triangle along the dotted line, does one half cover the other half completely?
video_script.why: The child learns to test a dotted line by folding, and to accept it as a mirror line only when one half covers the other exactly.
video_script.substitution: Fold the paper along the dotted line and see whether one half covers the other.
video_script.anchor: A blue triangle with a dotted line down its middle, beside four joined puzzle pieces with a dotted line through the middle
video_script.wrong_answer: any dotted line down the middle gives mirror halves
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says any dotted line down the middle gives mirror halves, because both sides look about equal. The folded puzzle pieces show a gap and an overlap, so the idea is struck out.
video_script.payoff_line: Only an exact match gives mirror halves.

final_answer.value: triangle: yes, mirror halves; puzzle pieces: no, not mirror halves
final_answer.spoken: the triangle halves cover each other, so they are mirror halves, but the puzzle halves do not fit, so they are not

never_show: a tick on the puzzle pieces before the fold
the verdict before the answer beat
maths_rules: Blue triangle with a dotted line down its middle: folding along the line puts one half exactly on the other, so they are mirror halves.
Four joined puzzle pieces with a dotted line through the middle: after the fold the bumps and holes do not meet, so the halves are not mirror halves.
Test: fold along the line and check that one half covers the other exactly.
A line that cuts a figure into mirror halves is a line of symmetry.
Slip: a line that looks as if it splits a shape evenly is not enough without the exact match.
video_script.design: One idea: mirror halves need an exact match after folding. Assumes the child can fold paper. Wrong idea: any dotted line down the middle gives mirror halves. The two book figures stay on the board from the hook to the end.
